claims.text: The initial alloy is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance that limits high-temperature use in air.
A dense Al2O3 coating approximately 2–5 µm thick will be deposited by PVD or CVD.
Applying an anti-oxidation coating is a relevant strategy for enabling high-temperature use of this refractory alloy system in air.
The Al2O3 coating will significantly reduce oxygen ingress into HfNbTaTiZr at high temperature.
The continuous, adherent Al2O3 layer will act as a physical barrier that prevents or strongly retards oxygen diffusion into the alloy matrix.
Al2O3 is thermodynamically stable at high temperatures.
Al2O3 has very low oxygen diffusivity.
The deposited coating will develop and maintain a protective scale during exposure at 1000 °C in air.
Suppressing oxygen ingress will minimize brittle surface-oxide formation and oxidation-induced deterioration.
The thin coating will not mechanically interfere with the bulk microstructure governing alloy strength and ductility.
After approximately 100 hours at 1000 °C in air, coated specimens will have lower oxidation mass gain and less surface degradation than uncoated specimens.
The coated alloy will retain a 1000 °C yield strength within 163–530 MPa at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The coated alloy will retain 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Coating adhesion under thermal cycling, possible spallation, coating-induced stress concentrations, and coating–substrate interactions remain unquantified.
